transcript:
This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Passengers on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv are describing what happened onboard the plane that caused them to make an emergency landing yesterday in Saudi Arabia.
That's after one of the pilots apparently stabbed the co-pilot while trying to crash the plane.
And Pierre's Kat Lonstorf reports 174 people were aboard.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu put out a statement after speaking with some of the passengers,
who described how several were able to enter the cockpit after the pilot, who was stabbed, unlocked its door while being attacked.
Those passengers then subdued the attacker.
One of them, named Yaniv Hanun, spoke to Netanyahu once back in Israel, his clothes still covered in blood.
He described putting the attacker in a chokehold and then pulling up on the controls to try to right the plane, something he'd seen in a TV show.
Several passengers, NPR interviewed, confirmed many of these details.
Israeli officials are calling it an attempted terrorist attack, although the motive is still unknown.
Kat Lonstorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth continues his reduction of the ranks of U.S. military generals and admirals.
This is happening as the war with Iran continues. And Pierre's Quill Lawrence says Hegseth announced the move yesterday in a speech to hundreds of junior military leaders in Virginia.
He says he's cut 10 percent of these flag officers already and would like to try to reach 20 percent.
And he smiled when he said in the past year these generals or admirals who disagreed with him aren't there anymore.
It's pretty unusual. Hegseth has been reaching way down into the promotion list to prevent some colonels from becoming generals
and just not giving any explanation.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reporting.
Cornell University says an outside counsel will investigate the school's handling of an alleged sexual assault case in 2024.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul had been calling for an independent investigation, as NPR's Brian Mann reports.
In a statement on social media, Hochul said she secured a promise from Cornell that the review by an outside counsel will happen.
And I just spoke to the university president. They have agreed. They understand the importance of this.
The university has drawn criticism for its response two years ago.
When word of an alleged sexual assault at a frat party first spread on campus after the woman reported it to campus police.
In a recent civil lawsuit, the woman alleges she was gang-raped by seven students.
None of the men faced criminal charges. Some were suspended or expelled.
But Cornell has declined to say what other disciplinary actions were taken.
Hochul says the probe is needed to restore trust.
I want answers. I want to know what happened.
No details yet on how the investigation will work. Brian Mann, NPR News, Ithaca, New York.
The state of Tennessee botched the execution of convicted murderer Christa Pike last night.
Executioners gave her a lethal dose of drugs twice.
Both attempts failed.
Witnesses say Pike was alive and snoring.
Tennessee officials moved Pike to a hospital.
This is NPR.
The Federal Trade Commission says it is investigating A.I. companies,
Anthropic, OpenAI and others, to find out if they're a risk to consumers.
Anthropic is a financial supporter of NPR.
In recent months, these companies have disclosed episodes where their A.I. agents have gone beyond human instructions
and humans didn't know about the actions right away.
OpenAI decided not to debut one of its new models because it failed testing standards.
Egg prices have fallen dramatically since early last year.
President Trump is often given his administration credit for that.
NPR's Joe Hernandez reports, egg experts say much of that decline has to do with avian flu.
An outbreak of avian flu that started in late 2024 was so severe that it resulted in the deaths of more than 50 million egg-laying hens in just six months.
The hit to the U.S. poultry supply caused egg prices to rise.
But since then, farms have been able to rebuild their flocks,
and they've enhanced their biosecurity protections with help from the Trump administration.
Poultry industry analysts say those efforts, plus a more recent milder avian flu season, have caused prices to drop again.
In August, egg prices were down 23 percent year-over-year, yet eggs were an exception.
Overall, grocery prices had increased by 2.2 percent.
Joe Hernandez, NPR News.
SpaceX has scheduled a Florida launch later this morning of its Crew-13 mission.
The four-person crew is scheduled to spend six months in orbit at the International Space Station.
This is NPR.
Stay tuned for the following announcements and messages from our sponsors.

topics.text: Pilot stabbed co-pilot on Dubai to Tel Aviv flight, made emergency landing in Saudi Arabia; passengers subdued attacker
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announces reduction of U.S. military generals and admirals by ten percent, aiming for twenty percent
Cornell University agrees to outside counsel investigation of alleged sexual assault case handling in 2024
Tennessee execution of convicted murderer Christa Pike botched; lethal drugs administered twice, both attempts failed
Federal Trade Commission investigating AI companies including Anthropic and OpenAI for consumer risk
Egg prices fallen dramatically since early 2024 due to avian flu outbreak killing fifty million hens
SpaceX scheduled to launch Crew-13 mission from Florida to International Space Station this morning
